amza-2021.title: Accelerated Aging Effect on Mechanical Properties of Common 3D-Printing Polymers
amza-2021.scope: FFF specimens: opaque blue Fillamentum PLA Extrafill and transparent natural PrimaSelect PETG; Creality Ender-3, Cura 4.5, 100% grid ±45° infill, 0.2 mm layers, two contours. PLA nozzle/bed: 205/45 °C; PETG: 235/65 °C. Unaged controls are discussed separately from UV-B-aged groups; ASTM D638-14 Type I dimensions, 1 mm/min, 23 °C / 50% RH, five specimens per tensile group. Ultimate strength is distinct from the supplier yield property.

fischbach-2023.title: Effect of physical aging on the flexural creep in 3D printed thermoplastic
fischbach-2023.scope: Author manuscript, printed BASF Ultrafuse PLA; 100% infill, 0.2 mm layers, 215 °C nozzle, 30 °C bed; ISO 899-2 bending creep. The long-duration test uses one specimen under a 10 N nominal force for 170 h near 20 °C. No family-wide lifetime or reduction factor is inferred. The long-duration specimen had an initial age of five hours; the authors report laboratory relative humidity of 30–50%.

This article uses only the initial-state PLA_100 relaxation cohort: 100% infill, a 2% tensile strain held for one hour, 20 ± 1 °C and 40% humidity. Table 5 reports maximum and one-hour residual stress; §2.2.4 defines the reported ± as standard deviation for five specimens. The hydrated cohorts, mass-normalized results and tensile-strength tables are outside this comparison. Residual stress at one hour is not an infinite-time equilibrium value.

outdoor-stratasys-pc-plaque-2-delta-e.definition: Reported CIE L*a*b* total color difference, exposed versus control; one source plaque result.
outdoor-stratasys-pc-plaque-2-delta-e.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 2, PC, Delta row, Plaque 2 ΔE column.
outdoor-stratasys-pc-plaque-2-delta-e.finding: Individual source result; no numerical acceptance threshold or measurement uncertainty is supplied.

fischbach-ultrafuse-pla-170h-creep-modul.definition: Flexural stress divided by time-dependent flexural strain at the end of the 170 h constant-load test; authors calculate strain from crosshead displacement and specimen geometry.
fischbach-ultrafuse-pla-170h-creep-modul.locator: §4.2, final paragraph after Figure 11; protocol §3.3 and strain/stress definitions §3.2, Eqs. 9–10.
fischbach-ultrafuse-pla-170h-creep-modul.finding: Author-reported final calculated modulus from one printed specimen; the specimen was still creeping at the end of the hold. No curve digitization or lifetime extrapolation is used.

liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-maximum-str.definition: Maximum tensile stress associated with applying the 2% strain before the one-hour relaxation hold; Table 5 labels this σmax. It is not ultimate tensile strength.
liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-maximum-str.locator: PDF p. 14, Table 5, PLA_100 row, σmax [MPa] column; test §2.2.1 and statistics §2.2.4.
liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-maximum-str.finding: Reported mean ± standard deviation for five specimens in the initial-state, 100%-infill cohort.

liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-one-hour-st.definition: Residual tensile stress after the one-hour hold at 2% strain. The source symbol σ∞ denotes this measured finite-duration endpoint here, not a demonstrated infinite-time limit.
liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-one-hour-st.locator: PDF p. 14, Table 5, PLA_100 row, σ∞ [MPa] column; one-hour endpoint defined in §2.2.1 on p. 6.
liber-knec-pla100-relaxation-one-hour-st.finding: Reported mean ± standard deviation for five specimens; the retained stress applies to the stated strain, environment, infill and specimen state.

tensile-test-scope.locator: Public Significance and Use §§4.1, 4.3–4.5 and Note 5; Scope §1.1 and Note 1.
tensile-test-scope.finding: Tensile properties depend on specimen preparation, rate and environment; modulus characterizes the initial response. Testing over different load durations and environments is needed for engineering use. ASTM D638 and ISO 527-1 have differing technical content.

stiffness-vs-strength.locator: §2 and Table 1 (materials and printing); §3.2, Table 2, PLA Control and PETG Control columns.
stiffness-vs-strength.finding: In the unaged control groups, the tested PLA specimens had a higher modulus while the tested PETG specimens had a higher ultimate tensile strength. This is an independent printed-grade result, not a yield-stress comparison or a statement about all PLA and PETG.

direction-and-load-path.finding: The guide connects FDM orientation to directional strength and recommends a short, direct load path. Its process-specific statements are not universal Z-strength data.

prusa-orientation.locator: Archive member Prusament PLA/1_PLA_Prusament_TDS_2022_EN.pdf, PDF p. 3, orientation sketch; corresponding PDF p. 3 sketches in PETG, ASA and PC Blend sheets.
prusa-orientation.finding: The inspected source sketches show both tensile coupons with the long axis along X: Horizontal is flat XY, and Vertical xz is on-edge XZ. Those are not in-plane versus build-Z tensile tests. The corresponding series retain their own source locators.

creep-below-tg.finding: One printed Ultrafuse PLA specimen continued to creep under the long room-temperature bending hold below its glass transition. This evidence calls for a sustained-load check but does not supply a general lifetime prediction.

impact-test-scope.locator: Public Scope §1.1 and Notes 3–4; Significance and Use §§5.2, 5.7–5.9.
impact-test-scope.finding: Specimen preparation, notch, conditioning and failure type affect impact results. A no-break observation is not an unlimited impact resistance. Results from different impact methods and specimen configurations do not establish a common ranking.

industrial-tooling-context.locator: §1.4, printed p. 4, Volvo Trucks application context.
industrial-tooling-context.finding: The manufacturer documents industrial FDM use by Volvo Trucks for lifting devices and ancillary tooling. This passage does not identify the exact grade or load rating for each component.

hdt-is-load-and-time-specific.finding: ISO 75 uses a heated three-point-bending test under defined stress. Its result does not establish maximum use temperature, design performance or long-term endurance.

hdt-two-stresses.locator: Public Abstract, methods A and B.
hdt-two-stresses.finding: ISO 75-2 identifies 1.80 MPa for method A and 0.45 MPa for method B. They are different test stresses, not interchangeable HDT labels.

d648-is-not-iso75.locator: Public Significance and Use §5.1; Scope Note 3.
d648-is-not-iso75.finding: ASTM D648 limits extrapolation to other exposure conditions and says its results must not be compared with ISO 75-1/-2 results because their technical content differs.

vicat-is-penetration.finding: Vicat identifies a specified needle-penetration response during controlled heating, rather than the flexural deflection measured by HDT.

tg-by-dsc.finding: DSC assigns a glass-transition temperature from a heat-capacity step in the material’s amorphous region.

tg-by-dma.finding: DMA examines temperature- and frequency-dependent viscoelastic response. The glass transition spans a range; the reported assigned temperature depends on the technique.

annealing-changes-printed-pla.locator: Experimental Section: Materials, Fused Deposition Modeling, Annealing and Thermal Analysis; Results: Dynamic Mechanical Analysis and Heat Deflection Temperature Changes, Figures 13–14.
annealing-changes-printed-pla.finding: The printed True Red PolyLite PLA study links thermal history, crystallinity and HDT. Its separately specified annealed specimens are not the HT-PLA grade or a transferable annealing recipe.

htpla-annealing-protocol-gap.locator: PDF p. 3, Thermal Properties; PDF p. 5, annealing note; PDF p. 6, How to Make Specimens.
htpla-annealing-protocol-gap.finding: The table labels annealed results; the recommendation and general recipe are separate from an identified HDT specimen protocol.

prusa-thermal-basis-gap.locator: PDF p. 2, Typical material properties HDT rows, compared with the separate Mechanical properties of 3D printed testing specimens table and its footnote (3) on p. 3.
prusa-thermal-basis-gap.finding: The PC Blend sheet’s thermal rows are outside the explicitly printed mechanical table. Its tensile-coupon orientation and recipe are not established thermal-test conditions.

composite-pa6-axes.locator: Property-table footnote immediately before the FAQ.
composite-pa6-axes.finding: The supplier describes Z as layer-to-layer behavior. The linked TDS retains the XY/Z labels but does not document its Z specimen preparation. Store numerical units and FAQ conditioning numbers are not used.

composite-pa6-protocol.locator: PDF p. 1, dry/wet mechanical-table footnotes, specimen-printing settings and note above them.
composite-pa6-protocol.finding: Both mechanical groups were annealed at 100 °C for 16 h. The wet group subsequently underwent 48 h immersion in 60 °C water. Filament drying is a separate recommendation; actual dry-group residual moisture and test temperature are not specified.

composite-pa12-axes.locator: Property-table footnote immediately before the FAQ.
composite-pa12-axes.finding: The supplier describes Z as layer-to-layer behavior. The linked TDS retains the XY/Z labels but does not document its Z specimen preparation. Store numerical units and FAQ conditioning numbers are not used.

composite-pa12-protocol.locator: PDF p. 1, dry/wet mechanical-table footnotes, specimen-printing settings and note above them.
composite-pa12-protocol.finding: Both mechanical groups were annealed at 100 °C for 16 h. The wet group subsequently underwent 48 h immersion in 60 °C water. Filament drying is a separate recommendation; actual dry-group residual moisture and test temperature are not specified.

composite-pa12-formulation.locator: Product description under Professional-Grade Mechanical Strength and Dimensional Stability.
composite-pa12-formulation.finding: The manufacturer markets the material as a PA12-based long-chain copolyamide containing 10% carbon fiber. The TDS has inconsistent matrix terminology; no exact comonomer recipe is established.

composite-pccf-scope.locator: PDF p. 2 lower mechanical table and p. 3 specimen printing note/orientation drawing.
composite-pccf-scope.finding: The PC-based composite has yield and tensile-modulus measurements on flat and on-edge coupons. Both have length along X. Its mechanical rows provide neither true build-Z tension nor a matched moisture-conditioned dataset.

composite-pa12-annealing-discrepancy.locator: FAQ asking whether prints require annealing; compare V1.1 TDS p. 1 dry/wet footnotes.
composite-pa12-annealing-discrepancy.finding: The product-page FAQ recommends a ten-hour anneal whereas the mechanical-table footnotes state sixteen hours. This article follows the footnotes attached to the measured specimens.

composite-cure-application.locator: Why these Specific Polymaker Materials; final Example Components image captions.
composite-cure-application.finding: The manufacturer identifies Fiberon PA6-CF20 in CURE Mannheim steering hardware and aerodynamic cores produced by filament printing. No loads, validation margins or conditioning history are supplied, so this example cannot qualify another design.

composite-pa6-formulation.locator: Product description under Engineered for Demanding Applications.
composite-pa6-formulation.finding: The manufacturer identifies a PA6 matrix with a marketed 20% carbon-fiber fraction. The inspected description does not state the mass-versus-volume basis or fiber dimensions.

nylon-copa-protocol.locator: PDF pp. 2, 4 and 6: formulation; dry/wet mechanical-table footnotes; specimen drawing and preparation settings.
nylon-copa-protocol.finding: CoPA is a PA6/66 copolymer with no fiber reinforcement declared. Mechanical coupons were annealed at 80 °C for 6 h. The dry group had a further 48 h drying step with temperature unspecified. The wet group was immersed in 60 °C water for 48 h and averaged 6.16% moisture. No replicate count or interpretation of ± is supplied.

nylon-copa-uptake-scope.locator: PDF p. 2, moisture-absorption graph: condition above graph and equilibrium annotation below curve.
nylon-copa-uptake-scope.finding: The separate absorption graph is labelled 23 °C and 70% RH and gives equilibrium uptake as 2.82%. Specimen size, process, initial conditioning, sample count, equilibrium criterion and mass-calculation method are not reported for this curve. This is not the immersed mechanical group.

nylon-processing-versus-service.locator: Opening guidance; How to Moisture Condition, especially the annealing discussion.
nylon-processing-versus-service.finding: The supplier distinguishes dry filament during extrusion from moisture acquired by a finished part. It places annealing before moisture conditioning and explains that reheating can dry the part again. Suggested conditioning durations are guidance, without a grade-and-geometry-specific equilibrium criterion.

nylon-dimensional-example-scope.locator: Affects on dimensional accuracy; 40 mm cube / 100% infill description and the before/after image tables: Screenshot_2024-12-26_140227_1024x1024.png and Screenshot_2024-12-26_140314_1024x1024.png on cdn.shopify.com.
nylon-dimensional-example-scope.finding: Illustrations compare annealed cubes with a later moisture-conditioned state. Axis values are presented as maxima, not replicate means, and the exposure and measurement protocol are absent. The supplier says dimensional response depends on geometry, size and fill. Neither the individual observations nor the table total is a universal compensation factor.

nylon-bambu-ppa-scope.locator: PDF p. 3, composition and specimen printing note; p. 2, water-absorption row.
nylon-bambu-ppa-scope.finding: The named PPA-CF is described as semi-aromatic nylon with carbon fiber; fiber content is not given. Its uptake is 1.30% at 25 °C and 55% RH, with duration, absorption method and specimen preparation unspecified. The printed mechanical specimens were unannealed, but the TDS does not label a wet mechanical group or link that uptake condition to mechanical values.

nylon-bambu-wet-protocol-gap.locator: Parameters Comparison: dry/wet XY bending rows, separate absorption row, and testing-sample note immediately below.
nylon-bambu-wet-protocol-gap.finding: The page reports dry/wet flexural results for Bambu PPA-CF using fully filled concentric 80 × 10 × 4 mm bars. It does not provide the wet exposure, annealing route, mechanical test method, test temperature, rate or replicate count. The separate absorption-row environment cannot be assumed to define the wet flexural group.

nylon-siraya-unfilled-identity.locator: Description opening paragraph; Key Material Properties; Printing Considerations.
nylon-siraya-unfilled-identity.finding: Fibreheart PPA is explicitly marketed as pure polyphthalamide, so this is an unfilled PPA candidate rather than an inferred identity from a PAHT label. Its dry/saturated property list omits exposure and specimen preparation, and its annealing advice conflicts within the page. No conditioned design value follows from the marketing list.

nylon-siraya-protocol-gap.locator: Property Data; Preparing for Printing; Moisture Management.
nylon-siraya-protocol-gap.finding: The technical sheet distinguishes tensile stress at break under ASTM D638, but supplies no specimen orientation or conditioning for that tensile entry. ISO 62 is attached to absorption without the selected procedure or duration. Dry/wet HDT values have no reported conditioning route. It both proposes annealing and advises against it elsewhere.

outdoor-shared-protocol.locator: PDF p. 2, Procedure and Table 1; PDF p. 9, Table 4.
outdoor-shared-protocol.finding: ASA and PC used F900/T16 prints, ten upright ZX tensile coupons per condition, the same stated QUV cycle, and at least 40 h of 23 °C/50% RH conditioning before tensile testing. The report does not disclose lamp identity, spectral irradiance or UV-table uncertainty.

outdoor-asa-grade-scope.locator: PDF p. 14, UV Aging paragraph and Table 8.
outdoor-asa-grade-scope.finding: The UV cohort is described as natural color ASA in the paragraph and ivory ASA in Table 8; that naming discrepancy is retained. Results concern this Stratasys FDM grade and color cohort.

outdoor-pc-white-scope.locator: PDF p. 9, UV Aging paragraph and Table 5.
outdoor-pc-white-scope.finding: The PC UV cohort uses PC White on an F900 at 0.254 mm. UV stabilization and coatings are not identified for this tested grade; a different stabilized PC must be evaluated separately.

outdoor-color-plaques.locator: PDF p. 2, Procedure; PDF p. 7, Table 2, ASA and PC rows, Plaque 1 and Plaque 2 ΔE columns.
outdoor-color-plaques.finding: Two separately reported plaque color differences are available per grade after the common QUV exposure. The flat XY color specimens are separate from the upright ZX tensile specimens; there is no reported color acceptance criterion or uncertainty.

outdoor-petg-uvb-protocol.locator: §2, Materials and Methods, Table 1 and paragraphs before tensile methods.
outdoor-petg-uvb-protocol.finding: The transparent natural PrimaSelect PETG experiment specifies three cycles of 8 h at 310 nm/0.43 W·m−2·nm−1 and 50 °C followed by 4 h lamp-off condensation/cooling to 23 °C. The stated 24 h is total UV-on exposure, not an equivalence to the Stratasys chamber protocol.

outdoor-petg-appearance.finding: The exposed natural transparent PETG was observed to yellow and darken. No numerical ΔE, haze or transmission result is reported here.

outdoor-no-calendar-conversion.finding: A laboratory light test needs material-specific correlation before it represents an outdoor environment; an irradiance-based conversion of hours to years is inadequate. Concurrent controls support relative comparisons within a specified test.

outdoor-climate-dependence.finding: UV, wetness, temperature and pollutants vary with site, so durability ordering from one climate need not hold in another. Exposure locations should cover the intended service climates.

outdoor-stabilized-pc-grade.finding: Makrolon 2407 is explicitly UV stabilized and listed for injection molding. That identity cannot be assigned to unspecified PC filament or to Stratasys PC White.

outdoor-protected-pc-system.locator: PDF pp. 24–25, Exterior weathering performance, especially grade/color/coating table on p. 25.
outdoor-protected-pc-system.finding: Covestro discusses absorbers and hard coats for exterior Makrolon systems and illustrates dependence on substrate grade and color. The application context is a protected industrial component system, not an FFF coupon qualification.

fischbach-creep-control-and-measurement.locator: §2.1 (creep compliance), §3.2/Eqs. 9–10 (load and calculated strain), §3.3 (long hold), §5 final paragraphs (measurement limitations).
fischbach-creep-control-and-measurement.finding: The bending experiment maintains nominal force and measures increasing deformation. Compliance is strain divided by stress; flexural creep modulus is its reciprocal. Crosshead-derived strain and initial contact/load resolution affect the measurements; the authors discuss corrections and recommend improved force or direct strain measurement.

liber-knec-fixed-strain-protocol.locator: PDF pp. 5–7, §§2.2.1 and 2.2.4; p. 13 §3.3 and Figure 13; p. 14 Table 5.
liber-knec-fixed-strain-protocol.finding: The study holds tensile strain at 2% for one hour and records declining stress. All mechanical tests use 20 ± 1 °C and 40% humidity. The initial PLA_100 cohort is separate from the specimens incubated in Ringer’s solution. The reported finite-time residual stress does not establish long-term clamp-force retention.

amza-bolted-joint-removal-torque.locator: §2/Table 1 (exact grades and print settings); §2/Figure 2b (joint); §3.4/Table 4 and Figure 7c (seven-day torque observations).
amza-bolted-joint-removal-torque.finding: M6 assemblies with washers in printed Fillamentum PLA Extrafill and PrimaSelect PETG were initially tightened to 5.07 N·m. All tested assemblies required lower removal torque after seven days at 23 °C and 50% RH. The reported load is estimated from tightening torque and a screw coefficient; direct preload or retained stress was not measured. Removal torque is a joint-level proxy, not a fixed-strain relaxation curve.

prusa-chemical-protocol.finding: Material-profile FFF coupons in XY were immersed at about 23 °C for 1 h, 7 h, 24 h and 7 days before ISO 527 tensile and ISO 179 Charpy tests. Controls were printed under the same conditions; post-immersion drying and testing interval are unspecified.

prusa-asa-acetone-collapse.locator: ASA; tensile strength and Charpy impact paragraphs.
prusa-asa-acetone-collapse.finding: Prusament ASA specimens collapsed during acetone exposure, preventing the reported mechanical tests; acetone concentration and time to collapse are not specified.

prusa-petg-alcohol-response.locator: PETG; tensile strength and Charpy impact paragraphs.
prusa-petg-alcohol-response.finding: The supplier reports lower Prusament PETG tensile strength after seven days in IPA 99%; impact toughness also decreased. The graphs do not supply an exact tabulated retention value for this record.

prusa-pc-acetone-response.locator: PC Blend; tensile strength and Charpy impact paragraphs.
prusa-pc-acetone-response.finding: Prusament PC Blend tensile strength declined after 24 h in acetone, with further loss during longer exposure. The control Charpy results are instrument-limited nonbreak bounds, not exact retained impact values.

apium-peek-propylene-glycol.locator: Chemical Testing of 3D Printed PEEK Parts; chemical table and result bullets.
apium-peek-propylene-glycol.finding: For Apium PEEK 450 Natural, the supplier lists propylene glycol 99.5% as R (good resistance) in a minimum seven-day room-temperature immersion program. It reports no observed discoloration, peeling/delamination, weight or dimensional change, without resolution or retained-strength values. Prose states 24.5 °C; the table rounds this to 24 °C.

immersion-vs-esc.finding: ISO 175 evaluates liquid immersion without external restraint and directs environmental stress cracking to the ISO 22088 series. An unloaded immersion test does not establish performance under assembly strain or sustained service stress.

kynar-mixtures-stress-permeation.locator: Factors affecting chemical resistance; Operating parameters; Permeability and tensile strength retention.
kynar-mixtures-stress-permeation.finding: Arkema identifies stress, temperature, concentration, mixtures and cycling as relevant and recommends actual-service trials. Its resin fuel-immersion and permeability guidance does not establish leak tightness or retained properties of a printed PVDF wall.

pp-gf30-candidate-scope.locator: Overview; Applications; Technical information / Chemical resistance.
pp-gf30-candidate-scope.finding: BCN3D offers PP GF30 as a chemically resistant filament for humid/aggressive environments and structural parts. The page does not publish a named-liquid qualification or retained-strength protocol. This filled grade is distinct from unfilled PP.

pom-stock-candidate-scope.locator: Product description; Main Features; Further processing options.
pom-stock-candidate-scope.finding: TECAFORM AH natural is an unfilled POM-C stock material offered for machining and described as resistant to cleaning agents. This does not qualify a POM filament for any specified cleaner.

pps-stock-candidate-scope.finding: TECATRON natural is an extruded unfilled PPS stock material with manufacturer chemical-resistance positioning. Its process and the absence of an exposure matrix prevent transfer of that claim to printed PPS or PPS-CF.
